title: A 700-Year-Old Pocket Notebook Was Found in a Toilet
mediaSource: medieval wax tablet notebook latrine Paderborn Germany archaeology

scenes.title: A 700-year-old notebook was found in a toilet
scenes.narration: Archaeologists excavating a medieval latrine in Paderborn, Germany, discovered a small portable notebook roughly the size of a modern smartphone.

scenes.title: It was a reusable medieval notepad
scenes.narration: The notebook was made from ten wooden pages coated with wax, allowing its owner to write, erase, and reuse the surface again and again.

scenes.title: The toilet helped preserve it
scenes.narration: The sealed, extremely damp latrine created conditions that protected the wood and wax from fully decaying for centuries.

scenes.title: Latin writing still survives on the pages
scenes.narration: The full text is still being studied, but researchers have identified Latin writing, with some lines possibly used as erasable writing exercises.

scenes.title: Its owner may have been wealthy
scenes.narration: Fragments of silk were also found nearby, suggesting the notebook may have belonged to a merchant, cleric, or another relatively wealthy person.

scenes.title: A lost notebook became a time capsule
scenes.narration: What was probably an annoying accident in the Middle Ages turned into a remarkably preserved record of everyday life seven centuries later.
